subject: general
question: Flute instruments comes under which type of instrument category?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flute instruments** generally fall under the category of **"Sushira Vadya."**
 
• **"Sushira Vadya"** refers to **wind instruments in Indian classical music that produce sound by blowing air through a hollow tube.**
 
• **The flute,** also known as "Venu" in** Indian classical music,** is a popular example of a **Sushira Vadya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghana Vadya:**

 
 
• Ghana Vadya refers to percussion instruments in Indian classical music that produce sound by striking or shaking.
 
• Examples of Ghana Vadya include instruments like the mridangam and ghatam.
 
 
 
• **Sushira Vadya:**
 
 
• Sushira Vadya refers to wind instruments in Indian classical music that produce sound by blowing air into them.
 
• Flute instruments, such as the** Bansuri (a bamboo flute) or Venu, fall under this category. **
 
 
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:**
 
 
• Avanaddha Vadya is percussion instrument. Sound is produced by a stretched membrane, such as a drum. Membranophonic instruments act as skin-vibrators because they produce sound-waves by vibrations of a stretched skin or membrane when struck, plucked, or stroked.
 
• Examples of Avanaddha Vadya include instruments like the** **Tabla, Ankya, Alingya, Oordhwaka, and Damru.
